title: Access reconciliation engine and authorization edge middleware
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight access reconciliation engine plus an "authorization edge" middleware that provides consistent allow/deny decisions across API ingress, runtime gRPC surfaces, and the admin Console. This ticket covers the core evaluation path, reconciliation semantics (org-level vs project-level overrides), audit event enrichment, and a low-latency policy cache designed for P99 < 2ms on common reads.

Scope and responsibilities:
- Reconciliation engine: deterministic merge of multiple policy sources (org, team, project, resource tags, temporary grants). Must produce an explainable decision blob (decision, matching rules, score, evaluation id).
- Edge middleware: small binary that runs at API ingress, in Dedicated edge pods, and as a Console interceptor. Calls local cache, streams cache-miss lookups to the policy service, and attaches evaluation metadata to request context for downstream tracing.
- Audit integration: emit structured audit events (json-lines) with evaluation id, principal, input attributes, matched rules, and fallback reason. Events must be enrichable with SAML/SSO attributes (idp:email, groups).
- SSO/SAML mapping: normalize external identity attributes into internal role/subject expressions before evaluation. Must support mapping rules with precedence and revocation lists.

Design constraints and trade-offs considered:
1) Latency vs completeness: we default to a cached fast-path that only evaluates stable attributes (principal id, static role grants) and falls back to a synchronous evaluation for volatile attributes (resource-bound tags). This reduces p99 but can surface stale allows for up to cache-ttl unless invalidated.
2) Cache invalidation: push-based invalidation for grant changes (via audit events from control-plane). Fallback TTL is configurable per-tenant.
3) Determinism: reconciliation order is deterministic—explicit denies always win, local project allow can grant unless a deny from a higher-priority scope exists. Edge caches must be able to re-evaluate on mismatch with control-plane logs.
4) Explainability: every decision includes a concise rule path string so Console UI and incident playbooks can show why a request was blocked/allowed.

Acceptance criteria:
- API ingress p99 authz latency <= 2ms for cache hit, <= 30ms for cache miss (measured in dedicated benchmark harness).
- All evaluation events are written to the audit stream (kafka) with <50ms end-to-end delay under normal load.
- Console shows the full explainable decision for any evaluated request in the Authorization Trace panel.
- Security review sign-off obtained and SAML mapping tests passing for Okta and AzureAD test tenants.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Implement engine and small feature-flagged middleware in staging; deploy to canary hostpool (10% traffic).
2) Monitor the authorization-miss metric and audit-lag dashboard.
3) Gradually expand to Dedicated clusters and Console; enable server-side strict mode (no cached allow) behind an enterprise feature flag for high-security tenants.

Longer-term follow-ups (out-of-scope for this ticket): dynamic rule telemetry, machine-readable policy diffs for rollbacks, and an offline policy linter for admin safety checks.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Initial ticket created with architecture sketch. Linked to RBAC v2 kickoff doc in Confluence.

2026-03-03 - Architecture review with Security and Platform. Security requested explicit deny precedence and an audit enrichment schema; Platform requested a tiny edge binary (Go) with no gRPC dependencies to keep cold-starts small.

2026-03-05 - Prototype of reconciliation algorithm implemented (pseudocode in PR). Early benchmark: cache-hit median 0.6ms, p99 1.9ms on a t2-small-like harness. Raw results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-proto/pull/241 (WIP).
2026-03-07 - Design feedback from Console PM (Marta Liu): add explainable rule-path tokens that map to UI labels. Added field 'explain_path' to decision blob.

2026-03-09 - Blocker discovered: SAML role attribute naming varies across IdPs. Created temporary normalization rules and a follow-up ticket to centralize mappings. Added ENG-891000 as a TODO for the mapping service.

2026-03-12 - Integration test: Okta test tenant passes mapping rules; audit events appear in kafka topic 'authz-evals' with evaluation_id. Created canary flag and plan to enable 10% traffic next week.
